topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Under 19 NYCRR 175.25(a)(1), "advertising" and "advertisement" are defined to mean promotion and solicitation related to licensed real estate activity, including but not limited to advertising via which of the following?
choice_a: Mail, telephone, websites, e-mail, electronic bulletin boards, business cards, signs, billboards, and flyers
choice_b: Only print newspaper classified advertisements
choice_c: Only signage physically placed on the property itself
choice_d: Only cooperative broker-to-broker listing notices
explanation: 175.25(a)(1) broadly defines advertising/advertisement to include mail, telephone, websites, e-mail, electronic bulletin boards, business cards, signs, billboards, and flyers, among other media.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Under 19 NYCRR 175.25(a)(1), which of the following is expressly excluded from the definition of "advertising" and "advertisement"?
choice_a: Any statement made on a personal social media account, regardless of content
choice_b: Commentary made by a duly licensed salesperson, associate broker, or broker that is not related to promoting licensed real estate activity
choice_c: Communications sent only to existing clients
choice_d: Advertising placed in printed periodicals
explanation: 175.25(a)(1) excludes from the definition of advertising/advertisement any commentary by a licensee that is not related to promoting licensed real estate activity.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Under 19 NYCRR 175.25(a)(2), what is required for two or more persons to be considered a "team" for advertising purposes?
choice_a: All members must independently hold a real estate broker's license
choice_b: The team must be separately registered with the Department of State as its own brokerage entity
choice_c: At least one member must be an associate real estate broker or real estate salesperson, all must be associated with the same real estate brokerage, and they must hold themselves out or operate as a team
choice_d: The team must consist of at least three licensed members
explanation: 175.25(a)(2) defines a "team" as two or more persons, one of whom must be an associate real estate broker or salesperson, associated with the same brokerage, who hold themselves out or operate as a team.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Under 19 NYCRR 175.25(a)(4), a "logo" for advertising purposes is defined as:
choice_a: Any image used anywhere in an advertisement, including personal photographs
choice_b: Only a design formally registered as a trademark with the Department of State
choice_c: A watermark required on every digital advertisement
choice_d: A graphic mark used to identify a real estate broker, associate broker, salesperson, or team, but not a photograph of such person or team contained in an advertisement
explanation: 175.25(a)(4) defines "logo" as a graphic mark identifying a broker, associate broker, salesperson, or team, specifically excluding a photograph of such person or team.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Under 19 NYCRR 175.25(a)(5), for purposes of the advertising rules, "property" is defined to mean:
choice_a: Real property or shares of stock in a cooperative corporation
choice_b: Only single-family residential real property
choice_c: Any tangible or intangible asset a broker markets, including businesses
choice_d: Real property only, expressly excluding cooperative interests
explanation: 175.25(a)(5) defines "property" as real property or shares of stock in a cooperative corporation, so co-op shares are covered by the advertising rules.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Under 19 NYCRR 175.25(b)(2)(i), no property may be advertised unless:
choice_a: The property has been actively listed for at least 30 days
choice_b: The real estate broker has obtained authorization for the advertisement from the owner of the property, or as otherwise provided in the regulation
choice_c: The salesperson handling the listing has given verbal approval
choice_d: The Department of State has pre-approved the advertising copy
explanation: 175.25(b)(2)(i) requires that the broker obtain authorization from the property owner before advertising the property.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Under 19 NYCRR 175.25(b)(2)(ii), a real estate broker shall not advertise property that is subject to an exclusive listing held by another broker:
choice_a: Under any circumstances, even with the listing broker's permission
choice_b: Unless the advertising broker discloses the commission split to the public
choice_c: Without the permission of the listing broker
choice_d: Unless at least 90 days have passed since the listing began
explanation: 175.25(b)(2)(ii) prohibits advertising property subject to another broker's exclusive listing without that listing broker's permission.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Under 19 NYCRR 175.25(b)(2)(iii), photographs of property posted on a real estate broker's website:
choice_a: May be freely reused by any other broker for their own marketing purposes
choice_b: Must be taken exclusively by the listing broker in person
choice_c: Are automatically exempt from copyright protection when used for real estate marketing
choice_d: Shall not be used or reproduced without written permission from the copyright holder of such photographs
explanation: 175.25(b)(2)(iii) treats property photographs on a broker's website as proprietary information that cannot be used or reproduced without the copyright holder's written permission.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Under 19 NYCRR 175.25(c)(1), an advertisement must indicate that the advertiser is a real estate broker, or provide the name of the broker or brokerage, together with:
choice_a: Either the full address of the broker/brokerage or its telephone number
choice_b: The broker's Department of State license number in every instance
choice_c: A statement of the broker's total years of licensed experience
choice_d: A disclosure of the broker's current standard commission rate
explanation: 175.25(c)(1) requires an ad to indicate the advertiser is a broker (or give the broker/brokerage name) plus either the full address or the telephone number.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Under 19 NYCRR 175.25(c)(2), if an advertisement includes the name of an associate broker, salesperson, or team, what else must also be printed in the advertisement?
choice_a: The associate's individual Department of State license number
choice_b: The name of the real estate broker and/or real estate brokerage
choice_c: The client's name and written consent
choice_d: Nothing further is required beyond the associate's name
explanation: 175.25(c)(2) requires that whenever an ad names an associate broker, salesperson, or team, the broker's and/or brokerage's name must also be printed in the advertisement.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Under 19 NYCRR 175.25(c)(5), an associate real estate broker, salesperson, or team may provide which additional contact information in an advertisement?
choice_a: A personal home address only
choice_b: No additional contact information beyond the brokerage's own phone number
choice_c: Additional contact information, such as a post office box
choice_d: A third-party referral service's telephone number
explanation: 175.25(c)(5) permits an associate broker, salesperson, or team to provide additional contact information such as a post office box in an advertisement.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Under 19 NYCRR 175.25(c)(6), a residence may be advertised or used as a real estate office, provided that:
choice_a: It is located in the same municipality as the brokerage's principal office
choice_b: The broker has first obtained a local zoning variance
choice_c: The residence is owned, rather than rented, by the broker
choice_d: It is properly licensed by the Department of State
explanation: 175.25(c)(6) permits a residence to be used as an office provided it is properly licensed by the Department of State.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Under 19 NYCRR 175.25(c)(7), if a broker, associate broker, salesperson, or team provides a telephone number other than the brokerage's in an advertisement, the advertisement must:
choice_a: Clearly identify the type of such other telephone number, such as desk, home, or cell phone
choice_b: Omit the brokerage's own telephone number entirely
choice_c: Obtain prior Department of State approval for the alternate number
choice_d: List the alternate number in a smaller font than the brokerage's number
explanation: 175.25(c)(7) permits alternate telephone numbers in ads provided the ad clearly identifies the type of number, such as desk, home, or cell phone.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Under 19 NYCRR 175.25(c)(8), a real estate team, associate broker, or salesperson may use a logo different from that of their broker or brokerage, provided that:
choice_a: The Department of State has separately registered the alternate logo
choice_b: The name or logo of the real estate broker or brokerage is also printed in the advertisement
choice_c: The alternate logo is used only on business cards, never in other advertising
choice_d: The alternate logo predates the licensee's association with the broker
explanation: 175.25(c)(8) allows a different logo for a team, associate broker, or salesperson as long as the broker's or brokerage's name or logo is also printed in the ad.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Under 19 NYCRR 175.25(c)(9), an advertisement stating that a property is "in the vicinity of" a geographical area or territorial subdivision must:
choice_a: Omit any reference to neighborhood names entirely
choice_b: Use only the property's postal ZIP code to identify its location
choice_c: Include the name of the geographical area or territorial subdivision in which the property is actually located
choice_d: Reference only the applicable school district, never the neighborhood
explanation: 175.25(c)(9) requires that such advertisements include the actual name of the geographical area or territorial subdivision where the property is located, and prohibits using a misleading area name.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Under 19 NYCRR 175.25(d)(1), classified and multi-property advertisements are permitted to omit which of the following, so long as they still indicate the advertiser is a broker or provide the broker/brokerage name?
choice_a: The name of the real estate broker or brokerage entirely
choice_b: Any indication that the advertiser is a real estate broker
choice_c: An honest and accurate description of the property
choice_d: The license type of any associate real estate broker or real estate salesperson named in the advertisement
explanation: 175.25(d)(1) allows classified and multi-property advertisements to omit the license type of any named associate broker or salesperson.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Under 19 NYCRR 175.25(d)(3)(i), websites created and maintained by associate brokers, salespersons, and teams are permitted only if:
choice_a: They are duly authorized by their supervising broker to create and maintain such websites, which remain subject to the broker's supervision while the website is live
choice_b: The Department of State has issued a separate website license
choice_c: The website is hosted exclusively on the brokerage's own servers
choice_d: The website displays no more than ten listings at a time
explanation: 175.25(d)(3)(i) conditions permission for associate/salesperson/team websites on the supervising broker's authorization and ongoing supervision while the site is live.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Under 19 NYCRR 175.25(d)(3)(ii), the homepage of an associate broker's, salesperson's, or team's website generally must include:
choice_a: A link to the Department of State's license lookup page
choice_b: A link to the broker or brokerage website with whom the licensee is associated, unless the broker or brokerage does not have a website
choice_c: A pop-up disclaimer that must be dismissed on every visit
choice_d: A direct link into the local multiple listing service's back end
explanation: 175.25(d)(3)(ii) requires a homepage link to the sponsoring broker's or brokerage's website, unless that broker/brokerage has no website.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Under 19 NYCRR 175.25(d)(4), when must a broker, associate broker, salesperson, or team include the advertising-rule information required by these regulations in an e-mail to a client or potential client?
choice_a: In every single e-mail sent to that client, without exception
choice_b: Only in e-mails that reference a specific property listing
choice_c: In the initial e-mail; the information may be omitted from subsequent e-mails to the same recipient
choice_d: The rule does not apply to e-mail, only to print advertising
explanation: 175.25(d)(4) requires the required advertising information in an initial e-mail to a client or potential client, but permits its omission from subsequent e-mails to the same recipient.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Under 19 NYCRR 175.25(d)(6)(i), an advertisement referencing property subject to another broker's exclusive listing must clearly and conspicuously disclose the exclusive listing broker's name immediately after a required phrase such as:
choice_a: "Sponsored Content"
choice_b: "See Listing Agent for Details"
choice_c: No specific phrase is required, only the broker's name somewhere in the advertisement
choice_d: "Listing Provided by [name of exclusive listing broker]"
explanation: 175.25(d)(6)(i) requires disclosure of the exclusive listing broker's name immediately after one of several specified phrases, such as "Listing Provided by [name]."

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Under 19 NYCRR 175.25(d)(6)(ii), a broker, associate broker, or salesperson who pays a third party to advertise a property subject to another broker's exclusive listing must, in addition to the required exclusive-listing-broker disclosure, include:
choice_a: Words disclosing that the advertisement is a paid advertisement, using at minimum the word "advertisement" immediately following the advertising licensee's name
choice_b: A hyperlink to the third-party platform's full terms of service
choice_c: The exact dollar amount paid for the advertisement
choice_d: A disclaimer that the listed property may no longer be available
explanation: 175.25(d)(6)(ii) requires such paid advertisements to disclose, at minimum, the word "advertisement" immediately following the advertising licensee's name.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Under 19 NYCRR 175.25(e)(2), if any unlicensed individuals are named in advertising for a team, the advertisement must:
choice_a: Exclude the unlicensed individuals' names entirely
choice_b: Clearly and conspicuously state which individuals are real estate licensees and which are not
choice_c: Identify the unlicensed individuals only by first name
choice_d: Obtain the unlicensed individuals' notarized consent to be named
explanation: 175.25(e)(2) requires team advertising that names unlicensed individuals to clearly and conspicuously distinguish which named individuals are licensees and which are not.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Under RPL 442-c, a real estate broker's license may be revoked or suspended for a salesperson's violation of Article 12-A only if:
choice_a: Any salesperson associated with the broker violates the law, regardless of the broker's knowledge
choice_b: The salesperson has been licensed for less than one year at the time of the violation
choice_c: The broker had actual knowledge of the violation, or retains the benefits, profits, or proceeds of a transaction wrongfully negotiated by the salesperson after notice of the misconduct
choice_d: The violation occurs at the broker's principal office rather than a branch office
explanation: RPL 442-c shields a broker from discipline for a salesperson's violation unless the broker had actual knowledge of it, or retained the benefits of a wrongfully negotiated transaction after notice of the misconduct.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Under RPL 442-c, a broker who has any salesperson associated with the firm who has not secured the required license is:
choice_a: Subject only to a written warning from the Department of State
choice_b: Required to pay double the unlicensed salesperson's commissions to the Department of State
choice_c: Not subject to any penalty, since the salesperson bears sole responsibility
choice_d: Guilty of a misdemeanor
explanation: RPL 442-c makes a broker guilty of a misdemeanor for having any salesperson associated with the firm who has not secured the required license.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Under RPL 441-d, when a broker's license is revoked or suspended, what happens to the licenses of real estate salespersons associated with that broker?
choice_a: Each associated salesperson's license is also suspended, pending a change of association or the expiration of the broker's suspension period
choice_b: Salespersons' licenses are automatically and permanently revoked as well
choice_c: Salespersons may continue operating independently until their own license renewal date
choice_d: Nothing changes for the associated salespersons' licenses
explanation: RPL 441-d provides that revocation or suspension of a broker's license operates to suspend the license of each associated salesperson pending a change of association or expiration of the broker's suspension.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Under RPL 442-b, when a real estate salesperson's association with a broker is terminated for any reason, who must forthwith notify the Department of State?
choice_a: The salesperson exclusively
choice_b: The broker
choice_c: Neither party; the Department of State discovers the change automatically at renewal
choice_d: Only the salesperson's new broker, once a new association resumes
explanation: RPL 442-b requires the broker to forthwith notify the Department of State when a salesperson's association is terminated.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Under RPL 442-b, after a salesperson's association with a broker is terminated, the salesperson:
choice_a: May continue negotiating pending transactions independently for up to 30 days
choice_b: May act under the former broker's license for up to 90 days
choice_c: Shall not perform any act within the prohibitions of Article 12-A until again becoming associated with a licensed real estate broker
choice_d: Must immediately reapply for an entirely new salesperson's license
explanation: RPL 442-b bars a salesperson from performing any act within the article's prohibitions from termination until becoming associated with a licensed broker again.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Under 19 NYCRR 175.13, a real estate broker should not give, or offer to give, anything of value to influence or reward the actions of another broker's salesperson or employee:
choice_a: Under any circumstances whatsoever, even with the other broker's knowledge
choice_b: Unless the value given is under $50
choice_c: Unless approved in writing by the Department of State in advance
choice_d: Without the knowledge of that salesperson's or employee's own broker
explanation: 175.13 prohibits giving or offering anything of value to influence or reward another broker's salesperson or employee without that person's own broker's knowledge.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Under 19 NYCRR 175.1, a broker who receives money belonging to a principal must deposit it into a separate, special bank account within:
choice_a: Three business days, safeguarding it in a secure location to prevent loss or misappropriation until then
choice_b: 24 hours
choice_c: 10 business days
choice_d: 30 calendar days
explanation: 175.1 requires a broker to deposit a principal's money into a separate, special bank account within three business days, safeguarding it until deposited.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Under 19 NYCRR 175.1, accrued interest on a principal's money held in a broker's special bank account:
choice_a: Automatically belongs to the broker as compensation for handling the account
choice_b: Shall not be retained by, or for the benefit of, the broker, except to the extent it is applied to and deducted from earned commission with the consent of all parties
choice_c: Must be forwarded monthly to the Department of State
choice_d: Can never be applied to the broker's earned commission under any circumstances
explanation: 175.1 bars a broker from retaining accrued interest except to the extent applied to and deducted from earned commission with the consent of all parties.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Under 19 NYCRR 175.1, a broker holding a principal's money may place it only in:
choice_a: Any interest-bearing investment the broker chooses
choice_b: The broker's personal savings account, so long as it is clearly labeled
choice_c: A federally insured bank account, and not any other depository, fund, or investment
choice_d: A money market fund selected by the client
explanation: 175.1 requires that a principal's money not be placed in any depository, fund, or investment other than a federally insured bank account.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Under 19 NYCRR 175.2, within a reasonable time a real estate broker must:
choice_a: Provide only an annual summary of all transactions handled for the client
choice_b: Render an account only upon the client's written demand
choice_c: Retain unexpended client funds until the entire transaction has fully closed
choice_d: Render an account to the client and remit any money collected for the client that remains unexpended for the client's account
explanation: 175.2 requires a broker to render an account and remit unexpended money collected for the client within a reasonable time.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Under 19 NYCRR 175.7, a real estate broker shall make clear for which party the broker is acting, and shall not receive compensation from more than one party except:
choice_a: With the full knowledge and consent of the broker's client
choice_b: If the total combined compensation does not exceed the standard commission rate
choice_c: In commercial transactions only
choice_d: Compensation from more than one party is never permitted under any circumstance
explanation: 175.7 permits a broker to receive compensation from more than one party only with the full knowledge and consent of the broker's client.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Under 19 NYCRR 175.10, a real estate broker:
choice_a: May offer any property believed to be for sale, pending owner confirmation
choice_b: Shall never offer a property for sale or lease without the authorization of the owner
choice_c: May offer a property for sale based on an expired listing agreement
choice_d: May offer comparable neighboring properties without restriction
explanation: 175.10 flatly prohibits a broker from ever offering a property for sale or lease without the owner's authorization.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Under 19 NYCRR 175.11, a real estate broker may place a sign on a property:
choice_a: At any time, since signage is considered standard marketing practice
choice_b: Only after the property has been under contract for at least 10 days
choice_c: Only with the consent of the owner
choice_d: Only if the sign omits the broker's name
explanation: 175.11 provides that no sign shall ever be placed on any property by a broker without the owner's consent.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Under 19 NYCRR 175.12, if a real estate broker prepares (or supervises the preparation of) an instrument relating to the broker's employment or to a real estate transaction, the broker must:
choice_a: Retain the only copy in the broker's file for confidentiality
choice_b: File the instrument with the Department of State within 30 days
choice_c: Deliver a copy only if the parties request it in writing
choice_d: Immediately deliver a copy of the instrument to the party or parties executing it
explanation: 175.12 requires a broker to immediately deliver a copy of a broker-prepared instrument to the parties executing it.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Under 19 NYCRR 175.15, a real estate broker:
choice_a: Shall not be a party to an exclusive listing contract containing an automatic continuation of the listing period beyond its fixed termination date
choice_b: Must include an automatic renewal clause in every exclusive listing contract
choice_c: May automatically extend an exclusive listing for up to 30 days after expiration
choice_d: May extend a listing automatically with only the seller's oral consent
explanation: 175.15 prohibits a broker from being a party to an exclusive listing contract with an automatic continuation clause beyond its fixed termination date.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Under 19 NYCRR 175.19, a "net listing" agreement -- where a broker retains as commission the difference between the sale price and a specified net amount promised to the seller -- is:
choice_a: Permitted only for commercial property transactions
choice_b: Prohibited; no broker shall make or enter into a net listing contract for the sale of real property or any interest therein
choice_c: Permitted with the seller's written informed consent
choice_d: Permitted so long as it is disclosed to the buyer
explanation: 175.19 flatly prohibits brokers from making or entering into net listing contracts for the sale of real property or any interest therein.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Under 19 NYCRR 175.24(b), every exclusive residential-listing commission agreement obtained by a broker must have attached (or printed on the listing and signed or initialed by the homeowner), in type size of not less than six point, an explanation of the difference between which two types of listings?
choice_a: "Open listing" and "net listing"
choice_b: "Buyer's agency" and "seller's agency"
choice_c: "Exclusive right to sell" and "exclusive agency"
choice_d: "Multiple listing" and "pocket listing"
explanation: 175.24(b) requires a six-point-type explanation distinguishing an "exclusive right to sell" listing from an "exclusive agency" listing, attached to or printed on the commission agreement.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Under 19 NYCRR 175.24(c), if an exclusive residential listing is obtained by a broker who is a member of a multiple listing service, the listing agreement must give the homeowner:
choice_a: No say in how offers on the property are submitted
choice_b: The right to opt the listing out of the multiple listing service entirely
choice_c: The option to accept only all-cash offers
choice_d: The option of having all negotiated offers submitted either through the listing broker or through the selling broker
explanation: 175.24(c) requires such listing agreements to give the homeowner the option of having negotiated offers submitted through either the listing broker or the selling broker.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Under 19 NYCRR 175.27, nothing in Part 175 is intended to be, or should be construed as, an indication that:
choice_a: A salesperson is either an independent contractor or an employee of a broker
choice_b: A broker's liability for a salesperson's conduct is limited
choice_c: Continuing education requirements are waived for any licensee
choice_d: There is a maximum permissible commission rate
explanation: 175.27's disclaimer clarifies that nothing in Part 175 should be read to classify a salesperson as an independent contractor or employee of the broker.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Under RPL 441-a(3), except as otherwise provided, each licensed real estate broker must:
choice_a: Maintain only a virtual office, with no physical signage requirement
choice_b: Have and maintain a definite place of business in New York and conspicuously post a sign on the outside of the building, readable from the sidewalk, indicating the licensee's name and business as a licensed real estate broker
choice_c: Post signage only if the broker operates more than one office
choice_d: Register the office location with the county clerk in lieu of posting a sign
explanation: RPL 441-a(3) requires a broker to maintain a definite place of business and post a readable sign on the building's exterior identifying the licensee's name and broker status.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Under RPL 441-a(5), a licensed broker who changes their principal business address must:
choice_a: Notify the Department of State orally within 24 hours
choice_b: Simply update the address on the next renewal application, with no separate notice required
choice_c: Give the Department of State written notice, accompanied by a $10 filing fee for each licensee named; an unnotified change suspends the license until the suspension is vacated
choice_d: Notify only the local county clerk of the change
explanation: RPL 441-a(5) requires written notice to the Department of State with a $10 fee per named licensee, and provides that an unnotified change suspends the license until vacated.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Under RPL 441-a(6), a real estate licensee's pocket card must contain:
choice_a: The licensee's Social Security number
choice_b: The licensee's home address only
choice_c: A record of the licensee's commission history
choice_d: The licensee's photo, name, and business address (and, for a salesperson, the name and business address of the associated broker); it must be shown on demand
explanation: RPL 441-a(6) requires the pocket card to contain the licensee's photo, name, and business address (plus the sponsoring broker's info for a salesperson), and requires it be shown on demand.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Under RPL 442-h(2)(b), a broker seeking to establish a new principal or branch office within an area subject to a Secretary of State nonsolicitation order must:
choice_a: Obtain prior approval from the Secretary of State
choice_b: Simply file a notice with the Secretary of State within 10 days after opening
choice_c: Obtain approval from the local real estate board instead
choice_d: No approval is required if the new office is a home office
explanation: RPL 442-h(2)(b) requires a broker to obtain the Secretary of State's prior approval before establishing a new principal or branch office in a nonsolicitation-order area.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Under 19 NYCRR 175.28(b), the Human Rights Law disclosure notice that a broker must ensure is provided to a prospective purchaser, tenant, seller, or landlord at first substantive contact may be delivered by email, text, electronic messaging, facsimile, or hardcopy, but:
choice_a: Only hardcopy delivery is acceptable under any circumstances
choice_b: Oral disclosure does not satisfy the requirements of this section
choice_c: The notice may be delivered orally if witnessed by a third party
choice_d: The notice is optional for purely commercial transactions
explanation: 175.28(b) lists permissible delivery methods for the disclosure notice but expressly states that oral disclosure does not satisfy the requirement.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Under 19 NYCRR 175.28(d), a signed acknowledgment of the Human Rights Law disclosure notice (or, if the recipient refuses to sign, a written declaration of the refusal) must be retained by the broker or licensee for:
choice_a: Not less than one year
choice_b: Not less than seven years
choice_c: Not less than three years
choice_d: There is no minimum retention period specified
explanation: 175.28(d) requires retention of the signed acknowledgment, or a declaration of refusal, for not less than three years.

topic: Advertising, Broker Supervision, and Office Operations
question: Under 19 NYCRR 175.29, a real estate broker must display the Department's Human Rights Law notice at every office and branch office, and where the broker also provides listings or postings in the office window, that notice must be:
choice_a: Kept in a binder available only upon a visitor's request
choice_b: Posted exclusively on the brokerage's website, not physically in the office
choice_c: Displayed only during business hours inside a locked case
choice_d: Prominently displayed in the window, visible to persons on the adjacent sidewalk
explanation: 175.29(a)-(b) requires the Human Rights Law notice to be prominently displayed in the office window and visible from the adjacent sidewalk when the broker also posts listings there.
